# Nashik to Trimbakeshwar Distance (and Back): km & Time
URL: https://nashiktourism.com/blog/trimbakeshwar-to-nashik-distance-route/

Distances and transport

# Nashik to Trimbakeshwar Distance (and Back): km, Time & Routes from Station, CBS and Ramkund

How far Trimbakeshwar is from Nashik, by starting point, with bus, jeep, cab and Kumbh 2027 notes. Same road in both directions.

By the NashikTourism.com Editorial Team · Last updated 22 Nov 2026 · Published 12 Apr 2026 · Last verified: Not yet verified against official sources

Quick answer

Trimbakeshwar is about 28–30 km from Nashik city (CBS) by road and about 36–40 km from Nashik Road railway station, the same in both directions. The drive is estimated at 45–60 minutes in normal traffic. These figures are reported by the sources named in the table, not yet measured by our editor.

How to read the figures on this page

Each figure carries its own status. Verified means an editor read the cited source and it supports the figure. Reported means the named sources publish it but an editor has not yet confirmed it. Sources differ means published figures disagree, so we show them all. Not yet verified means we have no supporting source yet. Routes, fares and timetables change; confirm with the operator before you travel. See how we mark what we know and our sources.

Dates, from our fact database: Mela opens 31 Oct 2026 · Amrit Snan 2 Aug 2027, 31 Aug 2027, 11 Sep 2027 (Nashik) and 12 Sep 2027 (Trimbakeshwar) · Mela concludes 24 Jul 2028. ◐Reported, not yet confirmed Dates and sources

Nashik to Trimbakeshwar and Trimbakeshwar to Nashik are the same road, so the distance is the same whichever way you travel. Trimbakeshwar, with its Jyotirlinga temple and the Kushavarta Kund, is also written Trimbak, Tryambakeshwar, Tryambakam, Trayambakam or Trambakeshwar; this guide covers all of them.

## How far is Trimbakeshwar from Nashik, by starting point?

The distance depends on where in Nashik you start. Nashik Road railway station is further than the city centre. Every figure below shows its own status: Reported means the named sources publish it but our editor has not measured it; Sources differ means the published figures disagree and we show all of them; Not yet verified means we have no supporting source yet.

For two of the most-searched starting points we have a full guide: Nashik Road railway station to Trimbakeshwar and Trimbakeshwar to Panchavati and Ramkund.

## Is Nashik to Trimbakeshwar the same distance as Trimbakeshwar to Nashik?

Yes. Both journeys use the same road, so the kilometres are the same. The time can differ, because it depends on traffic, the time of day and where in Nashik you start or finish. On busy festival and Amrit Snan days, allow far longer in either direction.

## Quick answers in Hindi and Marathi

### नाशिक ते त्र्यंबकेश्वर अंतर (मराठी)

नाशिक ते त्र्यंबकेश्वर किती किलोमीटर? नाशिक शहर (CBS) पासून रस्त्याने सुमारे 28–30 किमी, आणि नाशिक रोड रेल्वे स्थानकापासून सुमारे 36–40 किमी. सामान्य वाहतुकीत प्रवासाला साधारण ४५–६० मिनिटे लागतील असा अंदाज आहे (अद्याप पडताळलेले नाही).

त्र्यंबकेश्वर ते नाशिक हे अंतरही तेच आहे. हे आकडे प्रकाशित स्रोतांवर आधारित आहेत; आम्ही ते स्वतः मोजलेले नाहीत, त्यामुळे निघण्यापूर्वी नकाशा अ‍ॅपवर तपासा.

### नासिक से त्र्यंबकेश्वर की दूरी (हिंदी)

नासिक से त्र्यंबकेश्वर कितने किलोमीटर है? नासिक शहर (CBS) से सड़क मार्ग से लगभग 28–30 किमी, और नासिक रोड रेलवे स्टेशन से लगभग 36–40 किमी। सामान्य ट्रैफिक में सफ़र में लगभग 45–60 मिनट लगने का अनुमान है (अभी सत्यापित नहीं)।

त्र्यंबकेश्वर से नासिक की दूरी भी यही है। ये आंकड़े प्रकाशित स्रोतों पर आधारित हैं और हमने स्वयं नापे नहीं हैं, इसलिए निकलने से पहले मैप ऐप पर जाँच लें।

## How do you get from Nashik to Trimbakeshwar?

### By shared jeep

Shared jeeps are one way to travel between Nashik and Trimbakeshwar. Where they leave from, how often they run, how full they must be before leaving, and the fare have not been verified; ask locally or at your hotel.

### By MSRTC bus

MSRTC (the state transport corporation) is reported to run buses between Nashik and Trimbakeshwar from the Nashik CBS (Central Bus Stand). The Nashik Road station information page on erail describes the route as a bus to the CBS and then a bus to Trimbakeshwar (erail). We do not publish bus timings or fares because we have no verified timetable. Check departures, platform and the last return service with MSRTC (see our sources), and do not assume a late-evening return bus.

### By cab or taxi

A private cab gives door-to-door travel from anywhere in Nashik, including Nashik Road station and the airport. App-based intercity cabs list a Nashik to Trimbakeshwar route (Uber Intercity); availability and fares vary by day and demand, and we publish no fares. Ask your hotel or a local operator, and agree the fare (one way, or for a full day with waiting time) before you travel.

### By road (self-drive)

Use a current maps app for the route; the normal journey is estimated at 45–60 minutes (not yet verified) and can take much longer on busy days. Traffic and parking arrangements for the Mela have not been announced in sources we could locate, so check notices before you set out, and do not assume you can park close to the temple or the Kushavarta Kund on busy days.

## Is there a train to Trimbakeshwar?

We have not found a direct rail service to Trimbakeshwar. The nearest major station is Nashik Road (about 36–40 km by road, reported; see the table). The usual approach is to reach Nashik, by train to Nashik Road or by road, and continue to Trimbakeshwar by bus, jeep or cab. Confirm services on the railways’ own systems (Indian Railways, Central Railway and NTES). The full station-to-temple guide is at Nashik Road station to Trimbakeshwar.

## What do you pass between Nashik and Trimbakeshwar?

Places commonly mentioned along or near the route include:

- Gangapur Dam, near Nashik

- Anjaneri Hill, associated in tradition with Lord Hanuman

- Brahmagiri Mountain, traditionally associated with the source of the Godavari

- Trimbak town, at the end of the route, a pilgrim town

We have not verified distances to these places; check a maps app.

## How will Kumbh Mela 2027 affect the journey?

Nashik Kumbh Mela 2027 is reported to be held at two sites, Ramkund in Nashik city and Kushavarta Kund in Trimbakeshwar. Arrangements for the route during the Mela have not been announced in any source we could locate. Keep in mind:

- Traffic restrictions: no official parking, traffic or vehicle-restriction plan has been located. Restrictions are expected to be set by the police and the Authority and may change from day to day.

- Shuttles and special services: no shuttle-bus plan between Nashik and Trimbakeshwar has been found. The Railways say special trains are planned, but no numbers, routes or dates have been published.

- Journey time: it may increase a lot on busy days. We have no verified figure, so allow generous extra time.

- A possible strategy: consider visiting Trimbakeshwar on a different day from Nashik (Ramkund) rather than trying to do both on a busy date.

For dates, passes and the latest notices, use the Kumbh Mela 2027 hub and live updates. See also how to reach Nashik for Kumbh Mela 2027 and the reported snan dates.

## Which should you visit first, Nashik or Trimbakeshwar?

There is no single right order, and we have not found an official recommendation. If you arrive by train at Nashik Road station, it may be simpler to visit Nashik first, then travel to Trimbakeshwar, and return to Nashik for your onward journey. Check temple and Mela notices for both sites before you go.

## Places to visit around Nashik and Trimbakeshwar

- Trimbakeshwar Temple guide: the Jyotirlinga and Kushavarta Kund

- Panchavati and Ramkund and the Ramkund Ghat guide: the Nashik bathing site

- Sula Vineyards: wine tasting near Nashik

- Pandavleni Caves: the Buddhist caves

- Igatpuri: hill country on the Mumbai–Nashik corridor

- Bhandardara (Ahilyanagar district): Arthur Lake and waterfalls

### Staying in Trimbakeshwar?

Rooms may be limited around the Amrit Snan dates, so booking early is sensible. External site, with its own prices and terms.

## Frequently asked questions

### How far is Trimbakeshwar from Nashik Road railway station?

About 36–40 km by road, according to the sources named in the table (Nashik District tourism site, Housing.com and DistancesFrom). This is reported, not yet measured by our editor. Allow more time than the city figure, because Nashik Road is further from the Trimbakeshwar road than the city centre.

### How far is Trimbakeshwar from Nashik CBS?

About 28–30 km by road (reported). The Nashik District tourism site gives about 30 km from the city; our earlier guide gave 28 km without a source. Typical drive time is estimated at 45–60 minutes in normal traffic (not yet verified).

### How far is Trimbakeshwar from Ramkund or Panchavati?

We have no separate published figure. Ramkund is reported to be about 2 km from the CBS, so the city figure of about 28–30 km is a reasonable guide. See Trimbakeshwar to Panchavati and Ramkund.

### How far is Trimbakeshwar from Nashik (Ozar) airport?

Sources differ: most listings say about 40 km, one says about 55 km. Confirm which flights are operating before you plan around this airport, and pre-book a taxi.

### What is the last bus from Trimbakeshwar to Nashik?

We have no verified last-bus time and do not publish one. Ask at the Trimbakeshwar bus stand or check with MSRTC on the day, and do not assume a late-evening return bus. A shared jeep or cab is the fallback.

### Is there a train to Trimbakeshwar?

We have not found a direct rail service. The nearest major station is Nashik Road, about 36–40 km away (reported). Continue by bus, shared jeep or cab.

### How long will the journey take during Kumbh Mela 2027?

No verified figure exists. No official traffic or parking plan has been located, and the journey may take much longer than normal on Amrit Snan and other busy days. Allow generous extra time and check the live updates before you set out.

### What is the cheapest way to get from Nashik to Trimbakeshwar?

We have not verified fares for any option. An MSRTC bus from the CBS is the usual low-cost choice (reported); check fares with MSRTC, ask locally for shared vehicles, and agree any cab fare before you travel.

# Nashik Road Station to Trimbakeshwar: Distance and Options
URL: https://nashiktourism.com/transport/nashik-road-station-to-trimbakeshwar/

Transport

# Nashik Road Railway Station to Trimbakeshwar: Distance, Bus, Auto and Cab Options

The last leg from Nashik's main railhead to the Jyotirlinga, compared option by option.

By the NashikTourism.com Editorial Team · Last updated 22 Nov 2026 · Published 22 Nov 2026 · Last verified: Not yet verified against official sources

Quick answer

Nashik Road railway station is about 36–40 km from Trimbakeshwar by road, further than the city centre. The usual choices are a taxi direct, or a bus or auto to the CBS and then an MSRTC bus. We have no verified journey time, fare or last-bus time, so confirm before you travel.

How to read the figures on this page

Each figure carries its own status. Verified means an editor read the cited source and it supports the figure. Reported means the named sources publish it but an editor has not yet confirmed it. Sources differ means published figures disagree, so we show them all. Not yet verified means we have no supporting source yet. Routes, fares and timetables change; confirm with the operator before you travel. See how we mark what we know and our sources.

Most visitors reach Nashik by train at Nashik Road, the city’s main railway station, and many want Trimbakeshwar (also written Trimbak, Tryambakeshwar or Trayambakam) the same day. Trimbakeshwar has no direct rail service that we could find, so the last leg is by road. This guide compares the ways to do it. For the other starting points, see the Nashik to Trimbakeshwar distance guide.

## How far is Nashik Road station from Trimbakeshwar?

Road distance to Trimbakeshwar: Nashik Road station compared with the CBS

We have no separate figure for Old CBS; use this one as a guide and check a maps app from where you are standing. How we measured. Compiled on 22 Nov 2026 from the published sources named in each row. Not yet measured on a map by our editor, so no figure here is marked Verified. Always check the live route on a maps app for your own starting point.

The reported figures run from about 36 km to about 40 km depending on the source and the route counted. Because Nashik Road is several kilometres from the city centre, it is further than the CBS (about 28–30 km, reported). Trimbakeshwar to Nashik Road railway station is the same distance in the other direction.

## Which way should you go from the station?

Options from Nashik Road station to Trimbakeshwar

| Option | Best when | What we have not verified

| Taxi or cab direct | You have luggage, family or a tight schedule; fewest changes. | Fares and journey time. Agree the fare (one way, or a day trip with waiting time) before you set off.

| Bus or auto to the CBS, then an MSRTC bus | You want the lowest cost and can handle a change. | Bus numbers, departure frequency, fares and the last bus back. The change at the CBS adds waiting time.

| Shared jeep (from the city) | You are already in the city and are flexible on timing. | Where jeeps leave from, how often, and the fare.

| Pre-booked intercity cab | You arrive at an awkward hour. | Availability and fares; they vary by demand.

## How do you reach Trimbakeshwar by bus via the CBS?

The erail station page for Nashik Road describes the public-transport route as a bus from the station to the Nashik CBS (Central Bus Stand) and then a bus to Trimbakeshwar (erail). In practice:

- Leave the station and ask for the bus or auto to the CBS. We have not verified the station’s exits, bus bays or any prepaid counter, so check the signs on arrival.

- At the CBS, ask the enquiry desk for the Trimbakeshwar bus and platform. MSRTC publishes its own service information (see our sources).

- In Trimbakeshwar, confirm the last bus back before you queue for darshan. We do not publish a last-bus time because we have none that is verified.

## How long does it take from Nashik Road to Trimbakeshwar?

We have no verified journey time from the station. The city-centre drive is estimated at 45–60 minutes in normal traffic (not yet verified), and Nashik Road adds distance on top of that, so plan on more, and add a buffer for the change at the CBS if you go by bus. On busy days the time can be much longer.

## What changes during Kumbh Mela 2027?

Nashik Road is the station most Kumbh travellers are expected to use. The Railways describe special trains as planned (reported; no timetable located), and no official road-traffic, parking or shuttle plan for the Nashik–Trimbakeshwar route has been located. Expect crowds at the station and on the road on the reported Amrit Snan dates, and check live updates and the Kumbh Mela 2027 hub before you travel.

About 36–40 km by road (reported by the Nashik District tourism site, Housing.com and DistancesFrom; not yet measured by our editor).

### How do I get from Nashik Road station to Trimbakeshwar?

Take a taxi direct, or go by bus or auto to the Nashik CBS and then an MSRTC bus to Trimbakeshwar. Confirm bus details with MSRTC; we publish no timetable or fares.

### Is there a train from Nashik Road to Trimbakeshwar?

We have not found a direct rail service to Trimbakeshwar. Nashik Road is the nearest major station; continue by road.

### What is the last bus from Trimbakeshwar back to Nashik?

We have no verified last-bus time. Ask at the Trimbakeshwar bus stand or check with MSRTC on the day, and keep a taxi as a fallback.

# Trimbakeshwar to Panchavati and Ramkund: Distance and Options

Transport

# Trimbakeshwar to Panchavati and Ramkund: Distance, Bus, Jeep and Cab Options

Between the two Kumbh Mela sites: distance, options and what to check.

By the NashikTourism.com Editorial Team · Last updated 22 Nov 2026 · Published 22 Nov 2026 · Last verified: Not yet verified against official sources

Quick answer

Trimbakeshwar is about 28–30 km from Panchavati and Ramkund by road, close to the Nashik city figure, because the two are only a short way apart. Go by MSRTC bus via the CBS, shared jeep or cab. We have no verified time, fare or last-bus time; on Kumbh days allow far longer.

How to read the figures on this page

Each figure carries its own status. Verified means an editor read the cited source and it supports the figure. Reported means the named sources publish it but an editor has not yet confirmed it. Sources differ means published figures disagree, so we show them all. Not yet verified means we have no supporting source yet. Routes, fares and timetables change; confirm with the operator before you travel. See how we mark what we know and our sources.

Dates, from our fact database: Mela opens 31 Oct 2026 · Amrit Snan 2 Aug 2027, 31 Aug 2027, 11 Sep 2027 (Nashik) and 12 Sep 2027 (Trimbakeshwar) · Mela concludes 24 Jul 2028. ◐Reported, not yet confirmed Dates and sources

Panchavati and Ramkund, on the Godavari in Nashik, and Trimbakeshwar (also written Trimbak or Tryambakeshwar), are the two sites of Kumbh Mela 2027, and many pilgrims visit both. This guide covers the journey between them. The full distance table for other starting points is in the Nashik to Trimbakeshwar distance guide.

## How far is Ramkund from Trimbakeshwar?

Road distance to Trimbakeshwar from Ramkund, Panchavati and nearby
| Starting point | By road to Trimbakeshwar | Typical drive | Cheapest public option | Notes and sources

| Nashik CBS (Central Bus Stand) / Old CBS | About 28–30 km ◐Reported, not confirmed | About 45–60 min ○Not yet verified | MSRTC bus from the CBS (reported; confirm the platform and timings with MSRTC) | The usual reference point for "Nashik to Trimbakeshwar". We have no separate figure for Old CBS; use this one as a guide and check a maps app from where you are standing. Sources: Nashik District tourism site: Trimbakeshwar page (about 30 km from the city); NashikTourism.com earlier guide copy (28 km, no source cited)

| Panchavati / Ramkund | Roughly the city figure, about 28–30 km ○Not yet verified | Not yet confirmed | MSRTC bus from the CBS or Panchavati stand (reported; confirm with MSRTC) | We have not found a separate published figure for Ramkund. It is reported to be about 2 km from the CBS, so the city figure is a reasonable guide. See the Panchavati and Ramkund guide.

| Tapovan | Not yet confirmed ○Not yet verified | Not yet confirmed | Not yet confirmed | Near Panchavati. No published figure found; check a maps app.

| Kapaleshwar temple | Not yet confirmed ○Not yet verified | Not yet confirmed | Not yet confirmed | In the Panchavati area, so expect a figure close to the Ramkund one. No published figure found.

How we measured. Compiled on 22 Nov 2026 from the published sources named in each row. Not yet measured on a map by our editor, so no figure here is marked Verified. Always check the live route on a maps app for your own starting point.

We have not found a separate published figure for Ramkund or Panchavati. Ramkund is reported to be about 2 km from the Nashik CBS, so the city figure (about 28–30 km) is a reasonable guide. The distance is the same from Ramkund to Trimbakeshwar as from Trimbakeshwar to Ramkund. Tapovan and Kapaleshwar temple are in the same part of the city.

## How do you travel between Ramkund and Trimbakeshwar?

- MSRTC bus: MSRTC buses are reported to run to Trimbakeshwar from the Nashik CBS (erail). Our Ramkund guide and the transport hub note that the Panchavati bus stand is nearer Ramkund; whether Trimbakeshwar buses call there has not been verified. Timings, fares and the last bus back are not verified.

- Shared jeep: a common way to make the trip; pickup points, frequency and fare are not verified. Ask locally.

- Cab or taxi: door-to-door from your hotel in Panchavati. Agree the fare, and whether it includes waiting and the return, before you set off.

- Self-drive: use a maps app for the route; do not assume parking close to Ramkund or the temple on busy days.

## How long does the journey take?

The drive from the city is estimated at 45–60 minutes in normal traffic (not yet verified). We have no verified time specifically from Ramkund. Plan on more at peak hours, and much more on festival and Amrit Snan days.

## Can you do both Kumbh sites on the same day?

The reported third Amrit Snan has the Vaishnava akharas at Ramkund on 11 September 2027 and the Shaiva akharas at Trimbakeshwar on 12 September 2027 (reported, not confirmed; see the dates table on the Kumbh hub). No official traffic, parking or shuttle plan between the two has been located. On a busy date, consider seeing one site per day rather than both, and check live updates first.

## Frequently asked questions

### How far is Trimbakeshwar from Ramkund?

About 28–30 km by road, using the Nashik city figure as a guide (reported; no separate Ramkund figure found).

### How do I get from Ramkund to Trimbakeshwar?

By MSRTC bus from the CBS, shared jeep or cab. We publish no timetable or fares because none is verified.

### How far is Trimbakeshwar from Panchavati?

About the same as from Ramkund, roughly 28–30 km (reported guide figure; not separately confirmed).

### Can I visit Ramkund and Trimbakeshwar on the same day during Kumbh?

It is possible on quiet days, but no traffic or shuttle plan has been announced. On busy dates see one site per day and allow far longer.

Quick answer

The Nashik Kumbh Mela 2027 (Simhastha) is reported to open on 31 October 2026 and end on 24 July 2028, with Amrit Snan on 2 and 31 August and 11 and 12 September 2027 at Ramkund and Trimbakeshwar. These dates are reported, not yet confirmed by the Authority, and no general-visitor pass has been announced.

What is confirmed, and what is not

No date or figure on this page has yet been verified by our editors against an official notice. Items marked Reported come from credible reporting or an official page we have located but not yet re-read; items marked Sources differ show every figure with what it counts. The Authority’s own announcements are the source of truth — see our sources.

## The Kumbh at a glance

Short answers first; the detail follows.

What is it?

The Simhastha Kumbh Mela, one of the four Kumbh Melas held in rotation in India, held at Nashik and Trimbakeshwar on the Godavari when Jupiter is in Leo.

Where is it?

Ramkund in Nashik city (Panchavati) and Kushavarta Tirtha at Trimbakeshwar, about 28–30 km from Nashik city centre (not yet verified) — the two locations.

When is it?

Reported to open on 31 October 2026 (reported) and conclude on 24 July 2028 (reported). Main bathing dates: see the calendar.

Do I need a pass?

No general-visitor pass has been announced that we could locate. Passes and registration.

How do I get there?

By rail to Nashik Road, by road, or via Nashik (Ozar) Airport. Getting here and the transport hub.

What has changed recently?

We removed an unsourced Kumbh infrastructure figure (4 Oct 2026).

## Two locations: Ramkund and Kushavarta

Unlike other Kumbh Melas, the Nashik Kumbh spans two sites about About 28–30 km (not yet verified) apart. See the Nashik to Trimbakeshwar distance and routes for the table by starting point.

### Ramkund, Nashik (Panchavati)

The principal bathing ghat on the Nashik side, associated with the Vaishnava akharas. In the Ramayana tradition, Rama bathed here during his exile.
Panchavati and Ramkund guide

### Kushavarta Tirtha, Trimbakeshwar

The sacred bathing tank at the source of the Godavari, beside the Trimbakeshwar Jyotirlinga temple, associated with the Shaiva akharas.
Trimbakeshwar guide

## Practical tips for crowded days

General advice for any large gathering — none of it depends on arrangements that have not been announced.

- Carry as little as you can, and keep valuables at your lodging.

- Agree a meeting point with your group before you leave, and keep each person’s phone number written down.

- Download offline maps — mobile data can be slow in large crowds.

- Wear simple clothes you can bathe in, and shoes you can walk a long way in.

- Follow the instructions of police and volunteers over anything you read online, including here.

## Accessibility at the Kumbh

Ramkund and Kushavarta are reached by steps, and arrangements for older and disabled pilgrims will be set by the Authority. We have not yet verified step-free routes, accessible toilets or assistance points. See Accessible Nashik for how we classify access, the questions to ask, and what we are collecting.

## What to pack for the Kumbh Mela

General packing advice from an independent site, not a list of official requirements. We have found no published rules on what may be carried into the Mela area, so check notices before you travel. On a bathing day, leave almost everything at your hotel.

Clothes

Expect standing in water, long walks and crowds. Light colours reflect heat and make you easier to spot for your group.

- 2–3 sets of light cotton clothing, plus one extra set for after the holy dip

- A light jacket or shawl for early mornings and after bathing

- Comfortable walking sandals or rubber chappals rather than shoes; rubber slippers for the ghat area

- Leave at home: jeans, leather shoes, expensive or sentimental clothing, heavy woollens (unless it is cold), synthetic fabrics that do not breathe

Documents and phone

Never keep documents in a back pocket or loose bag in a crowd. Mobile data may be slow on Amrit Snan days.

- Government photo ID (original and a photocopy) in a waterproof pouch

- Accommodation booking confirmation and a printed train or bus ticket

- Emergency contacts written on paper as well as saved offline; 112 is India’s single emergency number

- Phone fully charged, a power bank, a charging cable, offline Google Maps for Nashik and a waterproof phone pouch

- Some cash, but not a large amount

Health and hygiene

Ask your doctor or pharmacist what is suitable for you.

- ORS sachets, paracetamol, an antacid, antiseptic cream and bandages

- Personal prescription medicines (carry extra), sunscreen, mosquito repellent, eye drops

- A reusable water bottle, hand sanitiser, wet wipes, tissues and a small quick-dry towel

Ghat day bag

- One change of clothes in a waterproof bag, and a plastic bag for wet clothes

- ID in a waterproof pouch, a small amount of cash, phone and power bank

- Water bottle, ORS sachets and a few biscuits, a small towel, rubber chappals

- Leave at the hotel: laptop, camera, valuables, jewellery, excess cash and a heavy backpack

Water and food

Do not drink water directly from the Godavari or from unknown sources. The press has reported a healthcare plan with temporary facilities and ambulances on bathing days, but exact locations are not published, so carry your own water and ORS and do not assume a facility will be near you. Eat freshly cooked food from established stalls. This is general advice, not medical advice.

## Frequently asked questions

What does Simhastha mean?

The Simhastha Kumbh is held when Jupiter (Guru) is in Leo (Simha Rashi). In the traditional account, drops of amrit fell at Nashik, and bathing in the Godavari during this period is held to be spiritually meritorious.

When is the Nashik Kumbh Mela?

The Mela is reported to open with a flag-hoisting on 31 October 2026 and to conclude on 24 July 2028, with the main Amrit Snan dates reported for 2 August, 31 August and 11–12 September 2027. These dates are reported, not yet confirmed against the Authority’s own notice — see dates and sources.

Is there a charge to attend the Kumbh Mela?

We have not been able to confirm. Earlier versions of this guide said there is no charge; we have not found an official statement either way. Ask the Authority — see our sources.

Do I need a pass or to register?

No general-visitor pass or registration requirement has been announced in any official source we could locate. Registration has been reported for religious organisations and for student volunteers only. Read passes and registration and check with the Authority.

Is it safe to attend?

Safety arrangements are set by the Authority, the police and the district administration, and are not yet published in a form we can verify. Follow official announcements and the instructions of police and volunteers on the day. See safety, medical and emergencies.

Can foreign nationals attend?

We have found no announcement restricting foreign visitors, but have not been able to confirm the position with the Authority. Foreign nationals need a valid Indian visa to enter India — see our guide for international visitors.

# Nashik Kumbh Mela 2027 Snan Dates – Reported Bathing Calendar
URL: https://nashiktourism.com/blog/kumbh-mela-2027-all-snan-dates/

# Kumbh Mela 2027 Snan Dates — Reported Calendar

The Amrit Snan dates reported so far for Nashik and Trimbakeshwar, with other traditional calendar occasions listed for reference.

Kumbh MelaApril 202610 min read

By the NashikTourism.com Editorial Team · Last updated 22 Nov 2026 · Published 12 Apr 2026 · Last verified: Not yet verified against official sources

Quick answer

The Amrit Snan dates reported for Nashik Kumbh Mela 2027 are 2 August, 31 August, 11 September (Nashik) and 12 September (Trimbakeshwar) 2027. They come from media reports of the state announcement and are not yet confirmed against the Authority's own notice. Other bathing days have not been confirmed.

How current is this guide?

This guide was written before the Kumbh Mela’s official arrangements were published. Dates, figures, rules, fares, timings and facilities it describes have not been verified against official sources, and some may be out of date or wrong. Where it differs from the dates below, the dates below — which carry their sources — take precedence. See live updates and the official sources.

Dates, from our fact database: Mela opens 31 Oct 2026 · Amrit Snan 2 Aug 2027, 31 Aug 2027, 11 Sep 2027 (Nashik) and 12 Sep 2027 (Trimbakeshwar) · Mela concludes 24 Jul 2028. ◐Reported, not yet confirmed Dates and sources

One common misconception about Kumbh Mela 2027 is that there are only a few important bathing dates. The Simhastha Kumbh Mela is reported to run from 31 October 2026 to 24 July 2028, and devotees traditionally bathe on further auspicious days between the Amrit Snan dates. The full list of bathing days has not been confirmed.

💡 Key Insight

You do not have to come on Amrit Snan days. Many devotees regard bathing on any auspicious day (a Parva Snan) as holy. A visit on a non-peak date may mean smaller crowds and easier travel and accommodation, but no crowd, access or cost arrangements have been announced for any date.

## The 3 Most Important Dates — Amrit Snan

These are the dates reported for the Amrit Snan, traditionally the most crowded and most significant bathing days, on which the akharas bathe in procession. All of them are reported, not yet confirmed against the Authority’s own notice:

1st Amrit Snan

2 August 2027

Monday • Ashadh Somvati Amavasya • Reported

2nd Amrit Snan

31 August 2027

Tuesday • Amavasya (month name not confirmed) • Reported

3rd Amrit Snan

11–12 Sep 2027

Nashik (11 Sep) • Trimbakeshwar (12 Sep) • Reported

## Kumbh Mela 2027 Snan Calendar (Reported)

Below is a calendar of the reported Amrit Snan dates, together with other traditional calendar occasions listed for reference. Only the Amrit Snan dates have been reported by the media; we have not found any source that has announced the other rows as Mela bathing dates. Orange highlighted rows are the reported Amrit Snan days.

| — 2026 — Mela Opening —

| 31 Oct 2026 | Saturday | Dhwajarohan (flag-hoisting) — reported Mela opening; reported as a simultaneous flag-hoisting at Ramkund (Nashik) and Kushavarta Tirtha (Trimbakeshwar) | Opening (reported)

| — July 2027 —

| 17 Jul 2027 | Saturday | Karka Sankranti | Parva (unconfirmed)

| 18 Jul 2027 | Sunday | Guru Purnima / Ashadha Purnima | Parva (unconfirmed)

| 29 Jul 2027 | Thursday | Kamika Ekadashi | Parva (unconfirmed)

| — August 2027 —

⚠️ Note on Dates

The Amrit Snan dates above have been reported by the media; none has yet been confirmed against the Authority’s own notice. The other rows are traditional Hindu calendar occasions, not announced Mela bathing dates. The Authority may announce additional or modified dates. Please check the Authority’s own notices before your visit — see dates and sources, live updates and our sources.

## Which Date Should You Choose?

### For Maximum Spiritual Significance — Amrit Snan Days

August 2, August 31, and September 11–12, 2027 (all reported, not yet confirmed). These are the days on which the akharas traditionally bathe in procession and the atmosphere is at its most intense. Expect very large crowds; if you attend, plan to arrive well ahead of time and check the Authority’s notices for any timing or access rules, which have not been announced in sources we could locate.

### For a Peaceful Experience — Parva Snan Days

Other auspicious days between the Amrit Snan dates may see smaller crowds than the Amrit Snan days, but there is no crowd forecast and none of these days has been announced as a Mela bathing date. Purnima and Amavasya days are traditionally regarded as auspicious.

### For Pilgrims Who Cannot Travel in Peak Months

The Mela is reported to conclude on 24 July 2028. By tradition, Kartik month (October–November 2027) is regarded as especially sacred for bathing in any tirtha. Whether any organised bathing events are planned outside the reported Amrit Snan dates has not been announced in sources we could locate, so check the latest notices before planning a visit.

## Frequently Asked Questions

### How many bathing dates are there in Nashik Kumbh Mela 2027?

The full list of bathing dates has not been confirmed. Amrit Snan dates have been reported for 2 August, 31 August, 11 September (Nashik) and 12 September (Trimbakeshwar) 2027. Devotees traditionally bathe on further auspicious days between them, but we have not found a published list of those days.

### Can I visit Kumbh Mela 2027 after September 2027?

The Mela is reported to conclude on 24 July 2028. Whether there will be organised bathing events after the reported Amrit Snan dates has not been announced in sources we could locate. By tradition, Kartik month (October–November) is regarded as especially sacred for bathing; check the latest notices before planning.

### What is the difference between Amrit Snan and Parva Snan?

Amrit Snan (also known as Shahi Snan) is the term for the major bathing days on which the akharas traditionally bathe in procession. Parva Snan generally refers to bathing on days of Hindu calendar significance such as Purnima, Amavasya, Ekadashi and Sankranti. Many devotees regard both as holy. Only the Amrit Snan dates have been reported for this Mela; we have not found an announced list of Parva Snan dates.

Both Kumbh Mela sites are on one route. See Nashik to Trimbakeshwar distance, bus, jeep and cab, from Nashik Road railway station to Trimbakeshwar and between Trimbakeshwar and Ramkund.

# Nashik Kumbh Mela 2027 E-Pass & Registration – What Has and Has Not Been Announced
URL: https://nashiktourism.com/blog/nashik-kumbh-mela-e-pass-registration-2027/

# Nashik Kumbh Mela 2027 E-Pass & Registration — What Has Been Announced

Is registration mandatory? Is there an e-pass? What has been reported so far, what has not been announced, and how to avoid paying for a fake “pass”.

Kumbh Mela8 min read

By the NashikTourism.com Editorial Team · Last updated 22 Nov 2026 · Published 26 Apr 2026 · Last verified: Not yet verified against official sources

Quick answer

No e-pass or mandatory registration for general visitors to Nashik Kumbh Mela 2027 has been announced in the sources we checked on 22 November 2026. Registration so far covers religious organisations and student volunteers. The Authority's official website is reported live; check it, and do not pay anyone for a pass.

Official status as of 22 November 2026

No general-visitor e-pass or mandatory registration has been announced in the sources we checked on 22 November 2026.

Official website. Free Press Journal (4 Nov 2026) and Punekar News report that the Authority’s official Simhastha website is live and is the place for announcements; the address reported is simhasthamahakumbh.maharashtra.gov.in. Check that any link you are given matches the address on the Authority’s own channels. Sources: Free Press Journal; Punekar News.

What has opened. Online registration for religious and charitable organisations (84 had completed it by early September 2026, per Free Press Journal) and student “Kumbhdoot” volunteer registration (Punekar News).

Digital Kumbh Pass. The “KumbhDoot” AI framework is reported to include an optional, consent-based Kumbh Pass stored in DigiLocker, with a pilot planned before wider rollout (Punekar News). It is not described as a requirement to attend. Whether a mobile app is live has not been confirmed.

No pass or registration scheme has been announced

We could not locate any official announcement of an e-pass or registration requirement for general visitors. Registration has been reported only for religious organisations and student volunteers. Parts of this guide describe a scheme in expectation, not as announced fact. Be cautious of anyone selling a “pass” before the Authority announces one, and see passes and registration on the Kumbh hub.

Dates, from our fact database: Mela opens 31 Oct 2026 · Amrit Snan 2 Aug 2027, 31 Aug 2027, 11 Sep 2027 (Nashik) and 12 Sep 2027 (Trimbakeshwar) · Mela concludes 24 Jul 2028. ◐Reported, not yet confirmed Dates and sources

One of the most searched questions as Nashik Kumbh Mela 2027 approaches is: "How do I get an e-pass for Kumbh Mela 2027?" and "Is registration mandatory?" This guide sets out what has and has not been announced, so you can avoid being misled by outdated content or by anyone selling a “pass”.

📅 Current Status

We could not locate any announcement of an e-pass or registration requirement for general visitors to Nashik Kumbh Mela 2027. What has been reported is narrower: online registration for religious and charitable organisations and for student volunteers, and administrative approval for a Simhastha web portal and mobile app. The official Simhastha website has since been reported live (see the official-status box above); whether a mobile app is live has not been confirmed. The dates quoted on this page are reported, not confirmed. See passes and registration on the Kumbh hub.

## What Is the Kumbh Mela E-Pass?

An e-pass is, in general, a digital permit that organisers of large events may use to manage crowd flow, for example for vehicle entry into busy zones. No e-pass or registration scheme for general visitors to Nashik Kumbh Mela has been announced in any source we could locate, so this page cannot describe how one would work.

Whether any ticket, pass or charge will apply to attending the Mela or bathing at Ramkund or Kushavarta Kund has not been confirmed either way. Charges for particular services, such as parking, lodging or special access, are separate questions. Until the Authority says otherwise, treat anyone who tells you a pass is definitely required, or definitely not required, as unreliable, and check passes and registration on the Kumbh hub.

## Do You Need to Register for Nashik Kumbh Mela 2027?

For general visitors, no registration requirement has been announced in sources we could locate. That is not the same as a confirmation that none will be introduced, so check for notices before you travel.

What has been reported so far:

- Online registration (through a QR-based single window) for religious and charitable organisations

- Registration for student volunteers (“Kumbhdoot”)

- Administrative approval for a Simhastha web portal and Android/iOS mobile app; the website is now reported live, the app’s launch is not confirmed

None of these is a pass for ordinary visitors. Follow live updates and latest updates for changes.

## Who Might Need an E-Pass?

The Authority has not published a list of who would need a pass, and we have not found one for any group of general visitors. In particular, we located no announced pass or registration scheme for:

- Private vehicle owners — no vehicle pass, parking scheme or entry rule has been announced

- Tour operators and pilgrim groups — no group registration scheme has been announced

- Media and press, akhara and sadhu communities and Sadhugram camp organisers — we have not found published arrangements; ask the Authority directly

If you belong to one of these groups, or travel by any mode, do not assume either that a pass is needed or that it is not. Check the Authority’s own channels listed on our sources page shortly before you travel.

## If a Pass or Portal Is Announced

The Simhastha website has been reported live (address as reported: simhasthamahakumbh.maharashtra.gov.in), and a mobile app was reported as approved; we have not confirmed the app is live and cannot give you an app name we have verified. If a pass or registration is announced, how to apply will be set by the Authority.

- Do not rely on an address or app link sent to you in a message, a social-media post or an advertisement.

- Find the Authority’s own channels through our sources page and confirm there that a scheme exists before entering any personal details.

- This site is an independent guide. It does not issue passes or take registrations.

⚠️ Beware of Fake E-Pass Websites

Large events can attract scam websites and messages that claim to sell passes, registrations or special access. Because no general-visitor pass has been announced, we advise you not to pay anyone for a Kumbh Mela “pass” or to enter identity or payment details on a site you reached through a forwarded message or advertisement. Whether any official scheme would carry a fee has not been announced. To check what has actually been announced, use the Authority’s own channels listed on our sources page.

## Vehicle Entry Rules on Amrit Snan Days

No official parking, traffic or vehicle-restriction plan for the Mela has been located. Parking areas, one-way systems and vehicle restrictions are expected to be set by the police and the Authority and may change from day to day. What we can say from the sources we located:

- No distance limit for private vehicles near Ramkund, and no parking-zone or check-post arrangement, has been announced.

- The Railways say special trains are planned; no numbers, routes or dates have been published that we could locate.

- No shuttle-bus plan, from Nashik Road station, the bus stands or anywhere else, has been found in any source we could locate.

The practical advice: do not assume you will be able to drive close to the ghats on Amrit Snan days. Plan on public transport or parking far away, and expect to walk some distance. Check parking and roads and the latest notices before you travel.

## Step-by-Step: What to Do Now for Registration

- General pilgrim: No registration or pass has been announced for general visitors, so there is nothing to apply for at present. Check for notices before you travel, and plan your travel and accommodation early.

- Private vehicle owner: No vehicle pass or parking scheme has been announced. Watch for notices from the Authority and the police nearer the time.

- Tour operator / group organiser: No group registration scheme has been announced. Contact the Authority directly, using the channels on our sources page.

- International visitor: Visa and entry rules are set by the Government of India and are separate from anything the Mela may require; confirm them with the relevant Indian authorities. We have not found any Mela-specific registration for foreign visitors.

- Everyone: Follow live updates for changes. This page will be revised if a pass or registration scheme is announced.

### While You Wait — Book Your Hotel

No general-visitor pass has been announced. Rooms near the ghats may be limited on busy dates, so booking early is sensible.

Search Nashik Hotels

## Frequently Asked Questions

### Is Nashik Kumbh Mela 2027 registration mandatory?

No registration or pass requirement for general visitors has been announced in any source we could locate. Registration has been reported only for religious and charitable organisations and for student volunteers. We cannot confirm that none will be introduced, so check for notices before you travel.

### Where do I find reliable information about Nashik Kumbh Mela 2027?

An authority to plan and coordinate the Simhastha has been reported as established by the Government of Maharashtra. Our sources page lists the Authority pages we located. The official website has been reported live; a mobile app was reported as approved and its launch has not been confirmed.

### Will there be an e-pass for vehicles during Amrit Snan?

Nothing has been announced. No vehicle pass, parking plan or traffic plan has been located. Parking areas and vehicle restrictions are expected to be set by the police and the Authority and may change from day to day, so check the latest notices before you travel.

### Can I get an e-pass from a third-party website?

No general-visitor e-pass has been announced, so be very wary of any website or message offering one. We advise you not to pay anyone for a Kumbh Mela pass. If a scheme is announced, confirm it through the Authority’s own channels on our sources page, including whether any fee applies.

# How to Reach Nashik for Kumbh Mela 2027 – Train, Bus, Flight Guide

# How to Reach Nashik for Kumbh Mela 2027 — Train, Bus & Flight Guide

Travel Tips
8 min read

By the NashikTourism.com Editorial Team · Last updated 22 Nov 2026 · Published 5 Apr 2026 · Last verified: Not yet verified against official sources

Quick answer

You can reach Nashik by train to Nashik Road station, by MSRTC or private bus, by road from Mumbai and Pune, or by air to Nashik (Ozar) airport. Journey figures here are approximate and unverified, and no special-train or traffic plans have been announced, so check the operators before you travel.

How current is this guide?

Routes, journey times, fares and train or bus names in this guide come from our earlier research and have not been verified. The Railways say special trains are planned, but no train numbers, routes or dates have been located, and shuttle-bus arrangements have not been announced in sources we found. Check the operators before you travel: see the transport hub. See live updates and the official sources.

Dates, from our fact database: Mela opens 31 Oct 2026 · Amrit Snan 2 Aug 2027, 31 Aug 2027, 11 Sep 2027 (Nashik) and 12 Sep 2027 (Trimbakeshwar) · Mela concludes 24 Jul 2028. ◐Reported, not yet confirmed Dates and sources

Attendance estimates for Nashik Kumbh Mela 2027 vary widely and none is confirmed, but planning your journey early is sensible. Whether you're coming from Mumbai, Pune, Delhi or abroad, this guide covers the main ways of reaching Nashik and what to check before you travel. Journey figures here are approximate and not verified; confirm them with the operators (see our sources and the transport hub).

## Ways to reach Nashik

🚂

### By Train

Several express trains connect Mumbai and Pune with Nashik Road. Check names, numbers and timings with the railways.

🚌

### By Bus

MSRTC and private operators serve Nashik. Check routes, timings and fares with the operator.

✈️

### By Flight

Ozar Airport is the airport serving Nashik. Scheduled flights are unverified; check with the airlines.

🚗

### By Road (Drive)

About 2.5–3 hrs from Mumbai in normal traffic (approximate; not verified). Expect it to be slower on busy days.

## Reaching Nashik by Train

Train is a common way to reach Nashik, especially from Mumbai and Pune. The railway station most visitors use is Nashik Road Railway Station; from there you will need a local transfer to Ramkund ghat (distance and time not verified, so check current options).

### Trains from Mumbai and Pune to Nashik

Several express trains connect Mumbai and Pune with Nashik Road. We do not list train names or numbers here because they and their timings change. Check names, numbers, running days and timings on the railways’ own systems (see our sources). A fast train from Mumbai takes about 2.5–3 hours (approximate; not verified).

⚡ Booking Tip

Trains around the reported Amrit Snan dates (2 Aug, 31 Aug and 11–12 Sep 2027) may be in heavy demand, and seats may sell out. Booking windows are set by the railways, so check them on the railways’ own systems. The Railways say special trains are planned; no numbers, routes or dates have been published that we could locate. Check live updates and the railways’ own systems regularly.

### From Nashik Road Station to Ramkund / Trimbakeshwar

- To Ramkund (Panchavati): local autos, cabs and buses are the usual options; fares and journey times vary and are not verified here

- To Trimbakeshwar: shared or private vehicles and buses are the usual options; fares and journey times vary and are not verified here (see the transport hub)

- No shuttle-bus plan from the railway station to the ghats has been found in any source we could locate

## Reaching Nashik by Bus

Buses are another common option, especially for travellers from within Maharashtra.

### MSRTC (State Transport) Buses

MSRTC, the state transport corporation, runs buses to Nashik from many Maharashtra cities. Routes, frequency, fares and boarding points vary, so check them with MSRTC before you travel (see our sources).

### Private Buses

Private bus operators also serve Nashik from other cities and states. Check the operator, route and booking terms yourself, and book early for busy dates.

📍 Nashik Bus Terminals

The main stand is usually given as the Nashik CBS (Central Bus Stand), with the Panchavati bus stand nearer Ramkund ghat (not verified; confirm with MSRTC or your operator).

## Reaching Nashik by Flight

Ozar Airport serves Nashik and is about 25 km from the city (approximate; not verified). A new integrated terminal has been reported as administratively approved; an approval is not a completion date.

### Flights to Nashik (Ozar)

Whether scheduled commercial flights operate from Nashik (Ozar), on which routes and how often, is unverified here and set by the airlines and the airport operator. Check the airlines and the Airports Authority of India before planning around a flight to Nashik, and keep an alternative route in mind.

⚠️ For International Travellers

If flying from abroad, you can arrive through a major international airport such as Mumbai's Chhatrapati Shivaji International Airport and continue to Nashik by road or rail (see the sections above and the transport hub). Pre-book your Nashik hotel before landing.

## Reaching Nashik by Road (Self Drive)

If you're driving from Mumbai, the drive is about 167 km and takes about 2.5–3 hours in normal traffic (approximate; not verified). Use a current maps app for the route, and expect delays on busy days.

### Key Road Routes

- From Mumbai: about 167 km, about 2.5–3 hrs in normal traffic

- From Pune: about 210 km, about 3.5–4 hrs in normal traffic

- From other cities: check a current maps app for the route and time; we have no verified figures to give

- All figures are approximate and not verified; highway numbers and road conditions change, so we do not list them

⚠️ Kumbh Traffic Warning

Roads into Nashik may be very congested on the reported Amrit Snan dates. Traffic and parking arrangements have not been announced in any source we could locate; they are expected to be set by the police and the Authority and may change from day to day. Consider arriving a day or more before, follow police instructions and check local news before travelling.

## Top Travel Tips for Kumbh Mela 2027

01

### Book Everything Early

Train and bus seats and hotel rooms may be hard to get around the Amrit Snan dates. Booking early is sensible.

02

Arrive a Day Before

Consider arriving the day before Amrit Snan. Roads into Nashik may be very congested on the day itself.

03

Use Off-Peak Dates

Other bathing dates fall during the Mela besides the reported Amrit Snan dates. A date away from them may be quieter, though we cannot say how much. See dates and sources.

04

Download Offline Maps

Download Nashik city maps on Google Maps offline. Mobile data may be slow in large crowds.

05

Nashik vs Trimbakeshwar

Decide which site you want first. The third Amrit Snan is reported as the Vaishnava akharas’ snan at Nashik (Ramkund) and the Shaiva akharas’ snan at Trimbakeshwar (reported, not confirmed).

06

Light Packing Only

You'll be in large crowds. Leave valuables at your hotel. Carry a small waterproof bag for the ghat.

## Frequently Asked Questions

### Which is the nearest airport to Nashik?

Ozar Airport serves Nashik and is about 25 km from the city (approximate; not verified). Whether scheduled flights operate from it is unverified, so check the airlines. You can also fly into Mumbai and continue to Nashik by road or rail.

### How far is Nashik from Mumbai by train?

Nashik Road Railway Station is approximately 2.5–3 hours from Mumbai by fast train (approximate; not verified). Several express trains connect Mumbai with Nashik Road; check names, numbers and timings on the railways’ own systems.

### Will there be special trains for Kumbh Mela 2027?

The Railways say special trains are planned, including long-distance specials and short-distance MEMU services. No numbers, routes or dates have been published that we could locate. Check the railways’ own systems and live updates.

### What is the best time to arrive in Nashik for Amrit Snan?

Consider arriving the day before your chosen Amrit Snan date. Procession timings and road closures have not been announced in any source we could locate, so check the latest notices for both before you travel.

Both Kumbh Mela sites are on one route. See Nashik to Trimbakeshwar distance, bus, jeep and cab, from Nashik Road railway station to Trimbakeshwar and between Trimbakeshwar and Ramkund.

# Where to Stay Near Ramkund Nashik – Areas and Options | Kumbh Mela 2027
URL: https://nashiktourism.com/blog/where-to-stay-nashik-kumbh-mela/

# Where to Stay in Nashik During Kumbh Mela 2027 — Hotels, Dharamshalas & Tips

Hotels & Stay
7 min read

Quick answer

# Ramkund Ghat Nashik – History, Visiting Tips & Kumbh Mela
URL: https://nashiktourism.com/blog/ramkund-ghat-nashik-guide/

# Ramkund Ghat Nashik Complete Guide — History, Visiting Tips & Kumbh 2027

The sacred bathing ghat on the Godavari river. Heart of Nashik spirituality and Kumbh Mela 2027 site.

Nashik GuidesApril 20267 min read

By the NashikTourism.com Editorial Team · Last updated 22 Nov 2026 · Published 12 Apr 2026 · Last verified: Not yet verified against official sources

Quick answer

Ramkund is a sacred bathing ghat on the Godavari in Nashik's Panchavati area, traditionally believed to be where Lord Rama bathed during his exile. It is reported to be a main Kumbh Mela 2027 bathing site. Opening hours, aarti times and Kumbh-day arrangements have not been verified; confirm locally.

How current is this guide?

Opening hours, fees, facilities and arrangements in this guide have not been verified against the venue’s or authority’s own information, and can change on festival days. Check before you travel. See our sources.

Ramkund is one of the most sacred bathing ghats in Nashik and, according to reports, a main bathing site for the Kumbh Mela 2027. Located in the Panchavati area on the banks of the Godavari river, it draws pilgrims and visitors throughout the year. Attendance estimates for the Kumbh Mela vary widely and none is confirmed. This is where Lord Rama is believed to have bathed during his 14-year exile, which is why the water here is deeply revered by many devotees.

📅 Kumbh Mela 2027 at Ramkund

The Amrit Snan dates reported for 2027 are 2 August, 31 August and 11 September (with a Trimbakeshwar snan reported for 12 September). These dates are reported, not confirmed, and which snans take place at Ramkund, and access hours and procession timings on those days, have not been announced. See the dates section of our Kumbh Mela 2027 page and latest updates.

## History and Significance of Ramkund

Ramkund is not merely a bathing ghat — it is one of the most spiritually charged sites in the Hindu tradition. According to the Valmiki Ramayana, Lord Rama along with Sita and Lakshmana settled in the Panchavati forest near Nashik during their 14 years of Vanvas (exile). Ramkund is traditionally believed to be the spot where Lord Rama bathed in the Godavari. The word "Kund" means a sacred water body, and "Ram" refers to Lord Rama himself.

The ghat’s stone steps leading down to the river are commonly said to date from the Peshwa era, though this site has not verified the dates of its construction. Ramkund has been a place of pilgrimage for many generations, and it is one of the sites of the Kumbh Mela, which returns to Nashik in a roughly 12-year cycle.

Religiously, bathing at Ramkund is believed to wash away sins (papa), help ancestors attain mukti (liberation), and bring spiritual blessings. This is why the ghat is also used for the immersion of ashes (asthi visarjan) — the last rites for the deceased — as it is believed the Godavari carries the soul to liberation.

## Ramkund Ghat Timings

Ramkund is an open riverside ghat. This site has not verified its opening hours or aarti times, which are set locally and can change on festival days. Treat everything below as indicative only and check locally.

| Activity | Time | Notes

| Opening | Approx. 5:30 AM (not verified) | First bathers at dawn; check locally

| Morning Aarti | Times vary; check locally | Early morning is traditionally considered an auspicious time to bathe

| Mornings | Generally busier | Crowd levels are not measured by this site

| Afternoon | Generally quieter | May suit visitors who want to look around

| Evening Goda Aarti | Often listed at about 7:00–8:00 PM, around sunset (reported; varies by season) | A lamp ceremony on the river. See the aarti section below to confirm

| Closing | Approx. 9:30 PM (not verified) | Check locally

| Kumbh Amrit Snan days | Not announced | Access arrangements on snan days have not been announced

🌟 Best Time to Visit Ramkund

Many visitors find the morning aarti the most spiritually charged and visually striking time to visit; check locally for the aarti time. The evening aarti with diyas on the river is also beautiful and is often less crowded than the morning. Weekend mornings tend to be the most crowded non-Kumbh hours.

## What time is the Godavari aarti at Ramkund?

Travel listings most often give the evening Godavari (Goda) aarti at Ramkund as about 7:00–8:00 PM, and one says it is held daily ◐Reported, not confirmed. Another source says it is held around sunset and shifts a little with the seasons, so a fixed clock time may be wrong on the day. We found no timing published by the temple trust or the municipal corporation, so we do not state one as confirmed. Sources: Trawell: Ram Kund; EaseIndiaTrip: Ramkund guide.

How to confirm the aarti time

Ask at the ghat on arrival or at your hotel, check the official sources (the municipal corporation and the district tourism site, Nashik District tourism site: Ramkund), and add a buffer: arrive 30 minutes early for a place near the river. On festival days and Amrit Snan days the aarti timing and access may differ; none has been announced. Searches for the “Ram Ghat Nashik aarti time” usually mean this Ramkund evening aarti.

The ghat is described as open at all hours in some listings (Incredible India: Ramkund) and as roughly 5:30 AM to 9:30 PM in our earlier copy; the two differ ⚠Sources differ. Check locally.

## How to Reach Ramkund Ghat

### From Nashik Road Railway Station

Nashik Road Railway Station is about 8 km from Ramkund (distance not verified). Auto-rickshaws and taxis are the usual way to cover it; fares and journey times vary, so agree the fare before you set off. Road and parking arrangements near the ghat during the Kumbh Mela have not been announced; expect restrictions and some walking on busy days. See parking and roads and our transport page.

### From Nashik City Centre (CBS Bus Stand)

Ramkund is in the Panchavati area. Auto-rickshaws run between the CBS and Panchavati; fares and journey times vary, so agree the fare first. A separate Panchavati bus stand is said to be nearer Ramkund (not verified), and city buses may serve the area; check locally.

### From Trimbakeshwar

Trimbakeshwar is roughly 28 km away, with a journey commonly estimated at 45–60 minutes depending on traffic (both figures not verified). Shared jeeps and private taxis are commonly used; fares vary, so agree the fare before you go.

### By Walking (from Panchavati)

If you are staying in the Panchavati area, Ramkund is likely within walking distance, depending on your hotel. Ask your hotel for the exact walking route. The lanes near Ramkund are narrow and best navigated on foot.

## Rules at Ramkund Ghat

The points below are general etiquette, not official regulations. This site cannot confirm which rules local authorities or temple trusts enforce, so follow any signs and instructions you see on site.

- Photography: Usually fine in open areas, but do not photograph other bathers without permission. Signs on site take precedence.

- Clothing: Dress modestly. Whether changing facilities are available nearby has not been verified, so do not rely on them.

- Footwear: Footwear is commonly removed before going down the ghat steps; follow signs and what others do.

- Plastic: Please avoid single-use plastic near the river and carry your litter out.

- Food: Please be considerate about eating on the ghat steps, which are used for worship.

- Loud music / speakers: Please keep music and speakers off; the ghat is a place of worship.

- Immersion of idols: Any rules can change around festivals; check with the local authorities.

- Asthi visarjan (ash immersion): Families usually arrange the rites with local priests (pandas); ask locally about current requirements.

## Which temples are near Ramkund?

Ramkund sits in the heart of the Panchavati area, with several temples and sacred sites nearby. Published distances are mostly measured from the Nashik CBS rather than between the sites, so the figures below show that; the sites are described as close together, but walking times have not been verified, so ask locally. Source for the CBS distances: Nashik District tourism site: Panchvati and Outlook Traveller: Panchavati; each figure is ◐Reported, not confirmed.

- Kalaram Temple — known for its black Ram idol, one of Nashik’s best-known temples; about 2.5–3 km from the CBS

- Sita Gufa — the cave where Sita is believed to have stayed during Vanvas; reported near Kalaram Temple, about 2.7 km from the CBS

- Sundarnarayan Temple — reported near the Ahilyabai Holkar bridge by Ramkund, about 2 km from the CBS

- Kapaleshwar Temple — reported to be across the river from Ramkund; no distance figure found

- Panchavati Banyan Tree — the banyan grove traditionally linked to the Ramayana’s Panchavati

- Ganga Ghat — another ghat on the Godavari, near Ramkund

- Muktidham Temple — white marble temple featuring replicas of India’s 12 Jyotirlingas

- Coin Museum — a museum devoted to coins; check its location and opening hours before planning a visit

Combine Ramkund with a day trip to Trimbakeshwar: see the Nashik to Trimbakeshwar distance and routes.

## Frequently Asked Questions

### Is Ramkund open every day?

Ramkund is an open riverside ghat and visitors come throughout the year. Hours of approximately 5:30 AM to 9:30 PM have been quoted, but they are not verified, and access can change on festival days or in bad weather. Check locally.

### What is the best time to avoid crowds at Ramkund?

Weekday afternoons are generally quieter, and weekday mornings are usually less crowded than weekends. Weekend mornings tend to be the busiest non-festival times. This site does not measure crowds, and they change with festivals and the season.

### Can non-Hindus visit Ramkund?

Ramkund is an open public ghat, and visitors of all backgrounds, including international visitors, generally come to see it. This site has not verified any rule about who may bathe or take part in rites, so ask locally and follow signs and the priests’ guidance.

### Is there parking near Ramkund?

Parking in the Panchavati area can be limited, and arrangements have not been verified. Parking and road arrangements for the Kumbh Mela have not been announced; expect vehicle restrictions and some walking on busy days. See parking and roads.

### What time is the aarti at Ramkund?

Travel listings most often give the evening Godavari aarti as about 7:00–8:00 PM, around sunset, but it varies by season and we found no timing published by the temple trust or the municipal corporation. Confirm locally on the day.

### How far is Ramkund from Trimbakeshwar?

About 28–30 km by road, using the Nashik city figure as a guide (reported, not yet measured by our editor). See the Nashik to Trimbakeshwar distance guide.

# Trimbakeshwar Temple, Nashik – Visitor Guide
URL: https://nashiktourism.com/discover-nashik/trimbakeshwar/

Spiritual · Jyotirlinga

# Trimbakeshwar Temple

Trimbakeshwar is a temple town in the hills west of Nashik, built around one of the twelve Jyotirlingas. It stands near the source of the Godavari, and during the Simhastha Kumbh Mela it is one of the two centres of the bathing rituals — the other being the ghats in Nashik city itself.

Information verified: not yet — see sources and verification. Timings may change during festivals. Confirm before travelling. Check with the official authority.

## Why visit Trimbakeshwar Temple

Trimbakeshwar is the reason a great many people come to Nashik district at all. The temple draws pilgrims through the year, and the town around it has grown up entirely in service of that visit — lodgings, priests, ritual supplies, queues.

It also feels quite different from Nashik city. The road climbs out of the plain into hills that stay green long after the monsoon, and the town is compact enough to walk. If you are making the trip from Nashik, it is worth allowing more time than the distance alone suggests.

## Things to see and do

The temple itself is the centre of any visit, and most people combine it with the tank at Kushavarta nearby, which is the bathing point associated with the Kumbh Mela at Trimbakeshwar. The surrounding town is small and easily explored on foot between visits.

## History and significance

Trimbakeshwar is counted among the twelve Jyotirlingas, the shrines to Shiva that hold particular importance in Hindu pilgrimage. Its position near the source of the Godavari ties it directly to the river that shapes the rest of Nashik — and to the Kumbh Mela, which follows that river down to the ghats at Ramkund.

## How to reach Trimbakeshwar Temple

Trimbakeshwar Temple is in Nashik district, Maharashtra. Nashik itself is reachable by train, bus, road and air, and our how to reach Nashik guide sets out the options from Mumbai, Pune and Delhi.

### From Nashik city

- Distance from Nashik city About 28–30 km ◐Reported, not yet confirmed

- Journey time from Nashik city 45–60 minutes ○Not yet verified

Check the transport hub for official sources before you travel.

## During the Kumbh Mela

Kushavarta Tirtha, beside the temple, is the Mela bathing point at Trimbakeshwar (Shaiva akharas).

Access, queues and crowd rules during the Mela will be set by the Authority and the police and may differ from ordinary days. We could not find a published plan for this site, so we do not describe one. See the Kumbh hub and live updates.

## Accessibility

?Accessibility unknown

Not yet verified by our editors. “Accessibility unknown” describes what we know, not the place — please ask before you travel. See Accessible Nashik.

## Best time to visit

Nashik's year divides fairly clearly into the monsoon, the cool months that follow it, and a hot stretch before the rains return. Our month-by-month guide to Nashik covers how that plays out across the district.

## Travel tips

- Temples in Maharashtra generally expect modest dress. It is worth checking current arrangements before you travel, particularly around festival dates.

- Queues lengthen considerably on auspicious days. If your dates are flexible, an ordinary weekday will be a very different experience from a festival one.

- Trimbakeshwar and Nashik city are separate destinations. Plan them as two trips rather than assuming you can fit both comfortably into a few hours.

## Frequently asked questions

Where is Trimbakeshwar?

Trimbakeshwar is a town in Nashik district, Maharashtra, in the hills to the west of Nashik city. Our route guide covers travel between the two.

Is Trimbakeshwar part of the Kumbh Mela?

Yes. The Simhastha Kumbh Mela at Nashik centres on two locations: the ghats at Ramkund in Nashik city, and Kushavarta at Trimbakeshwar. Our Kumbh Mela 2027 guide explains how the two connect.

Why is Trimbakeshwar significant?

It is one of the twelve Jyotirlingas, and it stands near the source of the Godavari — the river that the Kumbh Mela bathing rituals follow downstream to Nashik.

# Panchavati & Ramkund, Nashik – Visitor Guide
URL: https://nashiktourism.com/discover-nashik/panchavati/

Heritage · Ghats

# Panchavati & Ramkund

Panchavati is the old quarter of Nashik on the north bank of the Godavari, and Ramkund is the bathing ghat at its heart. It is the part of the city most closely tied to the Ramayana, and it is where the Nashik side of the Kumbh Mela takes place.

-
-
-
-
-
-
-
-
-
-
-

Location

North bank of the Godavari, Nashik city

Timings

Approx. 5:30 AM – 9:30 PM, year round
○Not yet verified

Entry

Not yet confirmed

Recommended duration

Not yet confirmed

Accessibility

?Accessibility unknown

Parking

Not yet confirmed

Official website

Not yet confirmed

Information verified: not yet — see sources and verification. Timings may change during festivals. Confirm before travelling. Check with the official authority.

## Why visit Panchavati & Ramkund

Panchavati is where Nashik stops being a modern city and becomes an old one. The lanes are narrow, the temples are close together, and the river is never far away. It is the densest, most atmospheric part of Nashik and the easiest place to spend a morning simply walking.

Ramkund itself is a working ghat rather than a monument. People come to bathe, to perform rites for the dead, and simply to sit. Visiting means joining that rather than observing it from outside, which is worth knowing before you arrive.

## Things to see and do

Ramkund is the anchor, and the temples of Panchavati sit within easy walking distance of it. The area is also the best eating in the city — our food guide to the area covers what to look for.

### What to eat near Ramkund

Food near the ghat and in the Panchavati lanes is largely vegetarian by custom. This site has not verified any rule about what may be sold there, so do not assume one; ask locally if it matters to you. Non-vegetarian food is more likely in other parts of Nashik city, such as the MG Road and College Road areas. Food-stall arrangements for the Kumbh Mela have not been announced.

- Nashik misal pav: spiced sprouted-lentil curry with farsan, onion and lemon, with bread rolls; a popular breakfast.

- Sabudana khichdi and poha with sev: light morning dishes; sabudana khichdi is eaten especially on fast days.

- Maharashtrian thali: dal, rice, vegetables, roti, papad, pickle and buttermilk at sit-down restaurants.

- Sweets from mithai shops in the lanes: chirote, shankarpali, puran poli, pedha; and cutting chai, strong milky tea in a small glass.

Small dhabas in the lanes around Ramkund are commonly said to serve early-morning pilgrims; opening hours and prices have not been verified, so ask before ordering. On fasting days, many eateries can serve fasting food; ask “upvaas ka khana hai?”. Earlier editions of our food guide named two restaurants (Satkar and Kapila); we have not re-verified their location, hours, menu or prices, so check before you go.

### Food safety on crowded days

General advice, not medical advice: eat freshly cooked, hot food at established stalls; avoid pre-cooked food sitting in the heat and cut fruit from unknown vendors on peak days; drink only bottled or sealed water; carry ORS sachets; and do not assume a stall is inspected, because no inspection arrangements have been announced. If you become unwell, seek medical help.

## History and significance

Panchavati is associated in the Ramayana with the years Rama spent in exile, and that association is what has drawn pilgrims here for centuries. Ramkund is the primary bathing point on the Nashik side of the Simhastha Kumbh Mela, which makes this quarter the focus of the city's Mela arrangements.

## How to reach Panchavati & Ramkund

Panchavati & Ramkund is in Nashik district, Maharashtra. Nashik itself is reachable by train, bus, road and air, and our how to reach Nashik guide sets out the options from Mumbai, Pune and Delhi.

Distance and journey time from Nashik city: not yet confirmed. See the transport hub and the how to reach Nashik guide.

## During the Kumbh Mela

Ramkund is the principal Mela bathing point on the Nashik side (Vaishnava akharas).

Access, queues and crowd rules during the Mela will be set by the Authority and the police and may differ from ordinary days. We could not find a published plan for this site, so we do not describe one. See the Kumbh hub and live updates.

## Accessibility

?Accessibility unknown

Ramkund is a working ghat reached by steps. During the Mela, access will be set by the Authority and may differ from ordinary days.

Not yet verified by our editors. “Accessibility unknown” describes what we know, not the place — please ask before you travel. See Accessible Nashik.

## Best time to visit

Nashik's year divides fairly clearly into the monsoon, the cool months that follow it, and a hot stretch before the rains return. Our month-by-month guide to Nashik covers how that plays out across the district.

## Travel tips

- Panchavati is best walked. The lanes are narrow and vehicle access near the ghat is limited, particularly during festivals.

- Ramkund is a place of active worship and of funeral rites. Photography is not always welcome — read the situation, and ask before pointing a camera at anyone.

- Mornings are the most active and the most interesting time at the ghat.

## Frequently asked questions

What is Panchavati known for?

It is the old riverside quarter of Nashik, associated in the Ramayana with Rama's years of exile, and home to Ramkund — the city's principal bathing ghat on the Godavari.

Is Ramkund where the Kumbh Mela bathing happens?

Ramkund is the main bathing point on the Nashik city side of the Simhastha Kumbh Mela. Kushavarta at Trimbakeshwar is the other centre.

Can I walk between the Panchavati temples?

Yes — the quarter is compact and most of it is easiest on foot. Our Ramkund guide goes into the area in more detail.

What time is the Godavari aarti at Ramkund?

Travel listings most often give the evening aarti as about 7:00–8:00 PM, around sunset, but it varies by season and we found no timing published by the temple trust or the municipal corporation. Confirm locally; see the Ramkund guide.

How far is Ramkund from Trimbakeshwar?

About 28–30 km by road, using the Nashik city figure as a guide (reported, not yet measured). See Trimbakeshwar to Panchavati and Ramkund.

# Igatpuri – Visitor Guide
URL: https://nashiktourism.com/discover-nashik/igatpuri/

Nature · Weekend

# Igatpuri

Igatpuri sits in the Western Ghats in Nashik district — hills, reservoirs and, through the monsoon, a great deal of water and green. This is the part of the district people come to for the landscape rather than the temples.

-
-
-
-
-
-
-
-
-
-

Location

Western Ghats, west of Nashik

Timings

Not yet confirmed

Entry

Not yet confirmed

Not yet confirmed

Accessibility

?Accessibility unknown

Parking

Not yet confirmed

Official website

Not yet confirmed

Information verified: not yet — see sources and verification. Timings may change during festivals. Confirm before travelling. Check with the official authority.

## Why visit Igatpuri

The Ghats change completely with the season here. Through the monsoon and just after, the hills are green, the streams are running and the cloud sits low over everything. It is a genuinely different landscape from the plain around Nashik city.

It is also the reason Nashik works as a weekend trip from Mumbai and Pune. A lot of people come out this way for the hills first and only discover the rest of the district afterwards.

## Things to see and do

This is a landscape rather than a list of sights. Most visits mean driving between viewpoints, walking where the weather allows, and stopping at the reservoirs. It rewards an unhurried pace more than a checklist. Bhandardara, with Arthur Lake and its waterfalls, is a separate trip just beyond the district line: see our Bhandardara guide (it is in Akole taluka, Ahilyanagar district, not Nashik district).

## History and significance

Igatpuri sits on the edge of the Western Ghats, where the plateau drops away westward. That escarpment is what makes the monsoon here so dramatic, and what has made this stretch a long-standing escape from the cities on the coast.

## How to reach Igatpuri

Igatpuri is in Nashik district, Maharashtra. Nashik itself is reachable by train, bus, road and air, and our how to reach Nashik guide sets out the options from Mumbai, Pune and Delhi.

Distance and journey time from Nashik city: not yet confirmed. See the transport hub and the how to reach Nashik guide.

## Accessibility

?Accessibility unknown

A hill landscape with limited public transport between points; access varies by viewpoint.

Not yet verified by our editors. “Accessibility unknown” describes what we know, not the place — please ask before you travel. See Accessible Nashik.

## Best time to visit

Nashik's year divides fairly clearly into the monsoon, the cool months that follow it, and a hot stretch before the rains return. Our month-by-month guide to Nashik covers how that plays out across the district.

## Travel tips

- The monsoon is the draw and also the difficulty — roads are wetter, visibility is lower, and paths are slippery. Plan accordingly.

- Weekends in season are busy. A weekday is a very different experience.

- This is hill country with limited public transport between points. Consider how you will move around before you commit to a route.
