# Bhandardara: Arthur Lake, Randha Falls, Fireflies and How to Reach
URL: https://nashiktourism.com/discover-nashik/bhandardara/

Nature and weekend trips

# Bhandardara: Arthur Lake, Randha Falls, Umbrella Falls, Fireflies and How to Reach

The lake, the falls and the fireflies in Akole taluka, Ahilyanagar district, with honest labels on every figure.

By the NashikTourism.com Editorial Team · Last updated 22 Nov 2026 · Published 22 Nov 2026 · Last verified: Not yet verified against official sources

Quick answer

Bhandardara is a lake and waterfall area in the Western Ghats, reported at about 70–73 km from Nashik, 156 km from Pune and 177 km from Mumbai. Its highlights are Arthur Lake, Randha Falls and, in the monsoon, Umbrella Falls; fireflies are reported from about May to June. These details are reported, not yet verified.

How to read the figures on this page

Each figure carries its own status. Verified means an editor read the cited source and it supports the figure. Reported means the named sources publish it but an editor has not yet confirmed it. Sources differ means published figures disagree, so we show them all. Not yet verified means we have no supporting source yet. Routes, fares and timetables change; confirm with the operator before you travel. See how we mark what we know and our sources.

Bhandardara is in the Western Ghats, in Akole taluka of Ahilyanagar (formerly Ahmednagar) district, Maharashtra. It lies close to the Nashik district boundary, not inside Nashik district, and is a common weekend trip from Mumbai, Pune and Nashik. It is often combined with Igatpuri, which is in Nashik district. Every figure below shows its status: Reported means published by the sources named, not yet confirmed by our editor.

Bhandardara key facts
| Fact | Answer | Status | Source

| Where it is | Akole taluka, Ahilyanagar (formerly Ahmednagar) district, Maharashtra; close to the Nashik district boundary | ◐Reported, not confirmed | Wikipedia: Bhandardara

| What it is | A lake and waterfall area around Arthur Lake, formed by Wilson Dam on the Pravara river | ◐Reported, not confirmed | Maharashtra Tourism: Bhandardara Dam

| From Nashik | About 70–73 km by road | ◐Reported, not confirmed | Trawell: About Bhandardara

| From Mumbai / Pune | About 177 km / 156 km (other sources give 165–185 km and 156–191 km) | ⚠Sources differ | Maharashtra Tourism: Bhandardara Dam

| Nearest railway station | Igatpuri, about 35–45 km away | ◐Reported, not confirmed | Holidify: How to reach Bhandardara

| Best time | Monsoon for the falls and greenery; October to February for pleasant temperatures; about May to June for fireflies | ◐Reported, not confirmed | Trawell: About Bhandardara

| Entry, timings, fees | Not yet confirmed | ○Not yet verified | No source linked yet

## What is Bhandardara known for?

### Arthur Lake and Wilson Dam

Arthur Lake is formed by Wilson Dam and fed by the Pravara river, and lies about 500 m from the Bhandardara bus stop, according to the sources named below ◐Reported, not confirmed. Opening hours, entry rules and any boating are not verified; ask locally.

### Randha Falls

Randha Falls is reported about 10 km from Bhandardara on the Rajur–Bhandardara road ◐Reported, not confirmed. Its flow depends heavily on the season; the monsoon is described as the best time to see it in full.

### Umbrella Falls

Umbrella Falls is reported to be seen during the monsoon, when the dam overflows ◐Reported, not confirmed. In dry months there may be little or no flow. Do not plan a trip around it without checking recent conditions.

### Kalsubai

Kalsubai, reported as Maharashtra’s highest peak, lies about 12 km from Bhandardara ◐Reported, not confirmed. Any trek is a physical commitment and conditions change with the weather; check with local operators and the forest department before you go.

## When is the fireflies season at Bhandardara?

Travel guides place the firefly display in the pre-monsoon window, roughly May to June, shifting with the arrival of the monsoon, and say it fades as regular rain sets in ◐Reported, not confirmed. Dates vary by year and there is no official calendar that we found. Reporting also links unsustainable tourism and habitat change to falling firefly numbers (Mongabay India), so watch from a distance, avoid torches and flash photography, and stay on paths. This is general advice, not an official rule.

## Igatpuri or Bhandardara: which should you choose?

Many visitors combine them, since Igatpuri is on the way from Mumbai. The table compares what the sources let us say.

Igatpuri compared with Bhandardara

| | Igatpuri | Bhandardara

| District | Nashik | Ahilyanagar (formerly Ahmednagar), Akole taluka

| What it is | Hill town in the Western Ghats, on the Mumbai–Nashik corridor ◐Reported, not confirmed | Lake and waterfall area around Arthur Lake ◐Reported, not confirmed

| From Nashik | About 45 km ◐Reported, not confirmed | About 70–73 km ◐Reported, not confirmed

| Nearest railway station | Igatpuri has its own station on the Mumbai–Nashik line ◐Reported, not confirmed | Igatpuri, about 35–45 km away ◐Reported, not confirmed

| Known for | Ghats scenery and monsoon greenery (see our Igatpuri guide) | Arthur Lake, Randha Falls, Umbrella Falls in the monsoon, Kalsubai peak, fireflies ◐Reported, not confirmed

| Choose it if | You want the hills close to the Mumbai–Nashik road or rail line. | You want a lake, waterfalls or a firefly evening and can spend the extra driving time.

## How do you reach Bhandardara from Nashik, Mumbai and Pune?

- From Nashik: about 70–73 km by road ◐Reported, not confirmed. Public buses and shared vehicles are reported; see the distance guide for how we label road figures.

- From Mumbai: roughly 165–185 km by road (the Maharashtra Tourism page gives 177 km); sources differ. The usual route is reported to run via the Mumbai–Nashik highway past Igatpuri.

- From Pune: roughly 156–191 km by road (the Maharashtra Tourism page gives 156 km); sources differ.

- By train: Igatpuri is the nearest station, about 35–45 km away, with buses or taxis onward ◐Reported, not confirmed. Check trains on NTES and IRCTC.

- By air: the nearest major airport is reported to be Mumbai, about 180–190 km away; Nashik (Ozar) airport is reported at about 90 km. Confirm which flights operate.

Use a live maps app for the route and current road conditions, especially on ghat roads in the monsoon. Our guide to reaching Nashik covers the Mumbai and Pune legs.

## Where can you stay near Bhandardara?

We list types of stay, not named properties, because we have not verified any listing, rate or availability:

- Lakeside and hillside resorts around Arthur Lake: the most common choice for weekend visitors.

- Homestays and village stays in the surrounding villages: often used for firefly season.

- Camping: offered by local operators; check safety arrangements, permission and the season.

- Stay in Igatpuri or Nashik and visit for the day: more transport options, longer journeys.

Weekends in season are busy. Book early and confirm directly with the property. Hotel search sites are external, with their own prices and terms: search Nashik-area hotels.

## What is the weather like, and how do you stay safe in the monsoon?

We publish no temperature or rainfall figures because we have none that is verified; use the India Meteorological Department. The monsoon is when the falls and the greenery are at their best, and also when roads, paths and rocks are at their most dangerous. This is general advice, not an official notice:

- Stay well back from waterfall edges and wet rock; do not enter fast or rising water.

- Water levels near a dam can change quickly. Follow local notices and instructions from police or forest staff.

- Ghat roads are slippery and visibility is low in cloud and rain; drive slowly and avoid night driving.

- Some trails and viewpoints may be closed in the monsoon. Check before you go, and do not trek without a local guide in heavy rain.

- In an emergency call 112 (see our sources).

## What else is nearby?

- Igatpuri: the hill town on the way from Mumbai

- Trimbakeshwar Temple, and the Nashik to Trimbakeshwar distance guide

- Sula Vineyards and Panchavati and Ramkund in Nashik

- Best time to visit Nashik and the two-day itinerary

## Frequently asked questions

### What is Bhandardara famous for?

Arthur Lake (formed by Wilson Dam), Randha Falls, Umbrella Falls in the monsoon, Kalsubai peak and the firefly season, all reported by Maharashtra Tourism and travel guides.

### When is the best time to visit Bhandardara?

The monsoon for waterfalls and greenery, October to February for pleasant temperatures, and about May to June for fireflies. Conditions vary by year; these are reported, not verified.

### How far is Bhandardara from Nashik, Mumbai and Pune?

About 70–73 km from Nashik, 156 km from Pune and 177 km from Mumbai by the Maharashtra Tourism figures; other sources give wider ranges (165–185 km from Mumbai, 156–191 km from Pune).

### Which district is Bhandardara in?

Akole taluka, Ahilyanagar (formerly Ahmednagar) district, Maharashtra. It is close to the Nashik district boundary but is not in Nashik district; Igatpuri is.

### Is Igatpuri or Bhandardara better for a weekend trip?

Igatpuri is closer to the Mumbai–Nashik road and rail line; Bhandardara is further in but has the lake and waterfalls. See the comparison table above.

### When is the fireflies season at Bhandardara?

Reported as roughly May to June, ending as the monsoon settles in. There is no official calendar we could find.

### Is Bhandardara safe in the monsoon?

The scenery peaks in the monsoon, but wet roads, slippery rock and fast water are real risks. Keep away from edges and fast water and follow local notices. This is general advice, not an official notice.

Wine · Leisure

# Sula Vineyards

Sula is the best-known name in Indian wine and the estate that made Nashik a wine destination. It sits in the hills outside the city, and it is open to visitors for vineyard tours and tastings.

## Why visit Sula Vineyards

A vineyard visit is the clearest illustration of how many different cities Nashik contains at once. You can spend a morning at the ghats in Panchavati and an afternoon on a terrace looking over vines, and the two feel like different countries.

Sula is also simply the easiest way into Nashik's wine country if you have never done it before. The estate is set up for visitors in a way that smaller producers are not, which makes it a sensible first stop before exploring further.

## Things to see and do

A visit generally means a walk through the vineyard, a look at the production side, and a tasting. The estate sits in open country outside the city, so allow time for the journey each way. Opening hours, prices and what is offered change, so check with the estate before you go.

### Wine tasting

Sula’s tasting room is described as overlooking the vineyards, with tasting sessions on offer. Packages, prices and which wines are poured vary, and it may be wise to ask about booking ahead on weekends. Check the minimum legal drinking age and carry ID if you plan to taste.

### Vineyard walk and dining

Walks through the vineyards may be available; ask whether guided walks run on the day you visit. The estate is understood to have restaurant and wine-bar options with vineyard views, and a resort stay on site. Which outlets are open, menus, room types, rates and availability have not been verified; check with the estate.

### SulaFest

SulaFest is the estate’s wine and music festival. Whether it is held in a given year, and on which dates, is announced by the organisers; this site has not confirmed any dates, format or ticket prices.

### Wines to know before you visit

Ranges and labels change, so ask the estate what is currently on offer. Names you may come across include The Source Sauvignon Blanc (a white), Dindori Reserve Shiraz (a red), Rasa Cabernet Sauvignon (a red), Brut (a sparkling wine) and Madera NV (a port-style dessert wine).

### How to reach Sula from Nashik

A cab (app-based where available, or a local taxi) is usually the simplest option from the city; auto-rickshaw fares are usually negotiated, so agree before you set off. If driving, head out of Nashik on Gangapur Road and use a maps app to find the estate. Fares and journey times vary and are not verified.

### Visiting Sula alongside Kumbh Mela 2027

A morning at Ramkund ghat followed by an afternoon at a vineyard is a distinctive combination. See our two-day Nashik itinerary for one way to structure it, and the Kumbh Mela 2027 hub for dates and arrangements.

## History and significance

The hills around Nashik hold the centre of India's wine industry, and Sula is the estate most responsible for that. Wine tourism is now one of the main reasons people visit Nashik who have no interest in its temples at all — which is a large part of what makes the city unusual.

## How to reach Sula Vineyards

Sula Vineyards is in Nashik district, Maharashtra. Nashik itself is reachable by train, bus, road and air, and our how to reach Nashik guide sets out the options from Mumbai, Pune and Delhi.

### From Nashik city

- Distance from Nashik city 15 km ○Not yet verified

Check the transport hub for official sources before you travel.

## Best time to visit

Nashik's year divides fairly clearly into the monsoon, the cool months that follow it, and a hot stretch before the rains return. Our month-by-month guide to Nashik covers how that plays out across the district.

## Travel tips

- A vineyard visit takes half a day once travel is counted. Do not plan it as an hour between two other things.

- If you intend to taste, sort out how you are getting back before you go.

- The cooler months are generally the most comfortable for an outdoor visit; the monsoon can make the setting lush and green, though rain may affect outdoor plans. Weekday mornings are generally quieter than weekends.

- The vineyards are at their most photogenic when the vines are in leaf. Our month-by-month guide covers how Nashik's seasons run.

## Nearby attractions

Heritage · Ghats
Panchavati & Ramkund
Panchavati is the old quarter of Nashik on the north bank of the Godavari, and Ramkund is the bathing ghat at its heart.

Spiritual · Jyotirlinga
Trimbakeshwar Temple
Trimbakeshwar is a temple town in the hills west of Nashik, built around one of the twelve Jyotirlingas.

Nature · Weekend
Igatpuri
Igatpuri sits in the Western Ghats in Nashik district — hills, reservoirs and, through the monsoon, a great deal of water and green.

## Frequently asked questions

Where is Sula Vineyards?

The estate is on the Gangapur Road side of Nashik, in the hills outside the city in Nashik district, Maharashtra. Confirm the exact address with the estate.

Do I need to book in advance for Sula Vineyards?

Booking rules are set by the estate and can change. Check with the estate before you go, especially for weekends and festival days, to find out whether advance booking is needed.

Is Sula suitable for non-drinkers?

The setting, grounds and dining can be enjoyed without wine tasting. What is open to non-drinkers, and whether any age rules apply to children, is decided by the estate, so check before you go.

What is the entry fee?

Entry arrangements and tasting prices are set by the estate and have not been verified by this site. Check with the estate before you go.

Is Nashik worth visiting just for the wine?

Plenty of people do exactly that. It is also easy to combine with the rest of the city — see our two-day itinerary.

# Editorial policy: how we verify what we publish
URL: https://nashiktourism.com/editorial-policy/

About this site

# Editorial policy

How NashikTourism.com decides what to publish, how it marks what it is sure of, and what it does when it is wrong.

## We are independent, not official

NashikTourism.com is an independent travel and information guide. We are not a government body, not the Nashik–Trimbakeshwar Kumbh Mela Authority, not a temple trust and not an official tourism organisation. Nothing here is an official notice. Where something is decided by an authority — Kumbh arrangements, temple timings, train schedules, road closures, entry rules — that authority is the source of truth, and we say so and link to it.

## Official sources come first

We rank sources. Official bodies (the Maharashtra Government, the Nashik district administration, the Authority, the railways, the police, an attraction’s own official site) come first. Established news is used to find out what is happening, and a news report becomes a fact on this site only when an official source supports it. A business’s own published information beats a third-party listing. Social media is never treated as confirmation. The full list, by tier, is on our sources page.

Important claims show where they come from: the name of the source, a link to it, when we last checked it, and when an editor last verified it. We do not write “according to sources”.

## How we mark what we know

Every fact that matters carries one of four labels:

✓Verified

An editor has read the official source we link to and it supports the statement. The date is shown.

◐Reported, not yet confirmed

Credible reporting, or an official page we have located, says so — but an editor has not yet confirmed it against the official source. Treat it as likely, not settled.

○Not yet verified

Carried over from earlier copy with no source behind it. Shown so you can see it, labelled so you do not rely on it.

⚠Sources differ

Sources disagree. We show every figure, with what each one counts and where it comes from, instead of picking one.

When we do not know something, we say Information not yet confirmed and point you to the official source. We do not fill gaps with a plausible guess: no invented dates, prices, timings, transport schedules, parking details, hotel availability, crowd numbers, rules, passes or official statistics.

## Dates and arrangements can change

The Simhastha Kumbh Mela is being planned in public and details evolve. Dates we show are labelled reported until the Authority’s own notice is linked. Timings at temples and ghats can change on festival days. Please confirm anything you are relying on, close to your travel date, with the official source.

## A person approves anything that could hurt you if it is wrong

Some information is high-stakes. Anything touching these areas is published only after a named human editor has approved it, whoever or whatever drafted it: accommodation availability, emergency, entry restriction, government order, kumbh rule, medical, pass registration, pricing, religious date, road closure, safety, traffic, transport restriction. Software that monitors sources may suggest an item, but it cannot publish one that falls in these areas, and it publishes nothing without review unless the site owner has explicitly changed that setting.

## Time-sensitive items expire

Updates that are only true for a while carry an expiry date. When it passes, the item moves to the archive automatically — it does not keep looking current. We keep the record rather than deleting it, so you can see what was said and when.

## Corrections

When we find a mistake, we correct it, say so, and keep a record. If you find one, please tell us and, if you can, point us to the official source. Corrections we have made:

- 4 October 2026Removed an unsourced government infrastructure figure; each reported development figure is now listed with what it counts and its source. — Kumbh Mela 2027 guide

- 4 October 2026Corrected the weekday of the second Amrit Snan date (31 August 2027 is a Tuesday) and relabelled the dates as 'reported' until the Authority's notice is linked. — Kumbh Mela 2027 guide

- 4 October 2026Withdrew the unsourced '15–20 crore' visitor estimate; no single official estimate is confirmed. — Kumbh Mela 2027 guide

- 4 October 2026Corrected the weekday of 31 August 2027 (Tuesday) and removed the 'Somvati' label that depended on it. — Kumbh Mela 2027 All Snan Dates

- 4 October 2026Added a notice that no general-visitor e-pass or registration requirement has been located in official sources. — Nashik Kumbh Mela E Pass Registration 2027

## Sponsored content, advertising and affiliate links

The site is supported by display advertising, affiliate links to booking sites and, where offered, sponsored content. How we keep that separate from editorial work:

- Sponsored content is always labelled. It carries a visible Sponsored tag and a disclosure line on the page, and every outbound link in it uses rel="sponsored nofollow".

- Sponsors never control the facts. A sponsor cannot pay for a recommendation, a ranking, a verification status or a change to a fact, and gets no preview or veto of editorial pages. Editorial guides follow the sourcing and approval rules above whether or not a sponsor is mentioned.

- A sponsored page is never marked Verified. Sponsored pages and sections carry no “Verified” status. Claims in them are the sponsor’s own, shown as such, and the site’s build fails if a sponsored block carries a Verified label.

- Affiliate links to hotel and booking sites are marked as sponsored in the page code. We may earn a commission at no extra cost to you. The surrounding text says they are external sites with their own prices and terms, and we do not take bookings or handle payments.

- No unmeasured claims. Advertising pages quote audience figures only when they come from a named measurement.

Advertising enquiries: Advertise with us.

## AI-assisted work

We may use AI tools to help draft, summarise, classify or extract information from sources. AI output is never treated as a source and never publishes anything on its own in the high-stakes areas above. Every item that appears on the site has been reviewed by a person; an AI summary of an official page is checked against the page itself before it is shown.

## Accessibility

We aim for WCAG 2.2 AA: keyboard operation, visible focus, readable contrast, descriptive image text and layouts that work from a 320px phone upwards. We never describe a place as accessible without verifying it — see Accessible Nashik. If something on this site is hard to use, tell us.
